idiom.title: Back to square one
idiom.interpretationEn: The idiom originates from the recursive nature of an old game or activity, where participants have to go back to the beginning whenever they make a mistake. In modern society, this saying is often used to indicate that after a failed attempt in a project or task, one has to start over again.
idiom.interpretationZh: 这个短语源于一项古老的游戏或活动的递归性质，当参与者出错时需要回到起点重新开始。在现代社会，这个成语常用以指某个项目或任务中的尝试失败之后，不得不从头再来。

examples.en: We took the wrong approach with this project, so it’s back to square one.
examples.zh: 我们在这个项目上采取了错误的方法，所以不得不重新开始。

examples.en: After the meeting, it seemed like we were back to square one with our plan.
examples.zh: 会议结束后，我们的计划似乎又回到了原点。

examples.en: Every time we think we’ve solved the problem, something else goes wrong and we are back to square one.
examples.zh: 每次我们以为解决了问题，都会再出些状况让我们回到原点。

people.name: Shimazu Tadatsune
people.bio: 16/17th-century Japanese warlord; leader of Satsuma Domain
people.extract: Shimazu Tadatsune  was a tozama daimyō of Satsuma, the first to hold it as a formal fief (han) under the Tokugawa shogunate, and the first Japanese to rule over the Ryūkyū Kingdom. As lord of Satsuma, he was among the most powerful lords in Japan at the time, and formally submitted to Tokugawa Ieyasu in 1602, to prove his loyalty, being rewarded as a result with the name Matsudaira Iehisa; Matsudaira being a branch family of the Tokugawa, and "Ie" of "Iehisa" being taken from "Ieyasu", this was a great honor. As of 1603, his holdings amounted to 605,000 koku.
highlights: First to hold Satsuma as a formal fief
First Japanese to rule over Ryūkyū Kingdom
Among the most powerful lords in Japan

people.name: Jacques Godbout
people.bio: Canadian novelist, essayist, children's writer, journalist, filmmaker and poet
people.extract: Jacques Godbout, OC, CQ is a Canadian novelist, essayist, children's writer, journalist, filmmaker and poet. By his own admission a bit of a dabbler (touche-à-tout), Godbout has become one of the most important writers of his generation, with a major influence on post-1960 Quebec intellectual life.
highlights: Canadian novelist, essayist, children's writer, journalist, filmmaker, poet
One of the most important writers of his generation
Major influence on post-1960 Quebec intellectual life

people.name: Fredric Warburg
people.extract: Fredric John Warburg was a British publisher, who in 1935 founded the company Secker & Warburg. He is best known for his association with the author George Orwell. During a career spanning a large part of the 20th century and ending in 1971, Warburg published Orwell's major books Animal Farm (1945) and Nineteen Eighty-Four (1949), as well as works by other leading figures such as Thomas Mann and Franz Kafka. Other notable publications included The Third Eye by Lobsang Rampa, Pierre Boulle's The Bridge over the River Kwai and William Shirer's The Rise and Fall of the Third Reich.
highlights: Founded the publishing company Secker & Warburg
Published George Orwell's Animal Farm and Nineteen Eighty-Four
Published works by Thomas Mann, Franz Kafka, Pierre Boulle
